questions.question: A routing facade is placed in front of a legacy monolith; each sprint one endpoint is reimplemented in a new service and the facade redirects calls to it, until the monolith can be retired untouched. Which migration pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Like the fig that grows around a host tree, the new system incrementally absorbs the old one's functions behind a facade until nothing is left to keep.

questions.question: Before bidding a maintenance contract, auditors compute cyclomatic complexity and Halstead volume per module and rank them by predicted change effort. What is this kind of upfront analysis called?
questions.explanation: Complexity analysis quantifies module intricacy with structural metrics so maintenance cost and risk can be forecast before committing.

questions.question: A 15-year-old system gains patches and workarounds every release, and with no deliberate redesign the code grows steadily harder to modify. Which of Lehman's laws of software evolution names this phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Lehman's second law: as an evolving system changes, its complexity increases unless work is actively done to reduce it.

questions.question: Modernizers find a self-contained pricing module inside a COBOL monolith, carve it out with its data, and repackage it as a callable service for the new platform. Which re-engineering technique is this?
questions.explanation: Component extraction isolates a cohesive slice of a legacy system and repackages it as a reusable, independently deployable component.

questions.question: A legacy payroll program is a single 20,000-line procedural listing; the re-engineering team groups related record operations into candidate classes before porting to Java. What is this transformation called?
questions.explanation: Object-oriented re-engineering recovers object structure - classes, encapsulation - from procedural legacy code as a bridge to an OO architecture.

questions.question: A 120-KLOC system logged 36 field defects during its first year in production. Compute its defect density in defects per KLOC.
questions.explanation: Defect density = defects / KLOC = 36 / 120 = 0.3 defects per thousand lines of code.

questions.question: A vendor must ship the same security fix for versions 2.4 and 3.1 at once because half its customer base has not upgraded. What is this arrangement of supporting several live releases simultaneously called?
questions.explanation: Parallel (multi-version) maintenance keeps several released versions alive at once, so each fix must be back-ported across every supported line.

questions.question: A team trains a model on five years of defect reports, change logs, and complexity trends to forecast which modules are most likely to fail next quarter. Which maintenance approach are they using?
questions.explanation: Predictive maintenance mines historical project data to anticipate failures and schedule work before users are hit - rather than reacting to incidents.

questions.question: A vendor announces version 5 will receive no further patches or support, yet thousands of deployments keep running it in production. What is version 5's lifecycle status called?
questions.explanation: End-of-life software is still operational but outside vendor support, accumulating unpatched risk until migrated or retired.

questions.question: What pattern translates between a legacy monolith's domain model and new microservices to keep them decoupled during migration?
questions.explanation: Anti-Corruption Layer isolates legacy systems from new ones during migration, translating between different models.

questions.question: A team snapshots legacy system outputs, refactors the code, then compares new outputs to detect behavioral drift. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Golden Master (approval) testing records trusted outputs and diffs them after changes to catch unintended behavior changes.

questions.question: During testing a team removes 240 defects before release; customers then report 60 more in the first quarter. Compute the Defect Removal Efficiency.
questions.explanation: DRE = defects removed pre-release / (removed pre-release + found post-release) = 240 / 300 = 0.80 = 80%.

questions.question: A fix must be applied to a running system without stopping it, as with OS kernels and embedded devices. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Hot patching modifies running code in place, eliminating downtime for critical always-on systems.

questions.question: A migration runs old and new implementations behind a toggle, first expanding then contracting the change surface. Which pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Expand-contract deploys the new structure alongside the old, migrates gradually, then removes the old path safely.

questions.question: The maintenance backlog holds 300 open defects against a two-engineer team; every Monday a board ranks each report by severity and business impact to choose the week's fixes. What is this practice called?
questions.explanation: Triage sorts the inflow of defects by severity and business value so scarce effort lands on the highest-impact fixes first.

questions.question: Despite doubling its maintenance staff, an organization's effective output rate stays nearly flat. Which of Lehman's laws predicts this invariant work rate?
questions.explanation: Lehman's 5th law (Conservation of Organizational Stability / invariant work rate) states a system's effective work output is largely invariant over its lifetime.

questions.question: A legacy system's documentation was lost; engineers analyze the code to reconstruct domain concepts and design rationale at a higher level of abstraction. This reverse-engineering activity.
questions.explanation: Design recovery recreates higher-level abstractions (design intent, domain knowledge) from code; redocumentation only regenerates documentation at the same abstraction level.

questions.question: Rather than rewriting a stable legacy system, the team hides it behind a new service interface and builds all new functionality around it. This maintenance/migration approach.
questions.explanation: Wrapping exposes legacy functionality through new interfaces while keeping the core intact - unlike the strangler pattern, it does not incrementally replace the system.

questions.question: Of 200 maintenance requests in a year, 110 add or enhance features, 36 port the system to a new OS, 40 fix defects, and 14 restructure code to prevent future faults. The percentage of effort spent on perfective maintenance.
questions.explanation: Feature enhancement is perfective maintenance: 110 of 200 requests = 55%. (Porting = adaptive, defect fixes = corrective, restructuring = preventive.)

questions.question: A full regression suite needs 9 days but the release window is 3; the team uses program dependence analysis to run only the tests whose outcomes could be affected by the change. This technique.
questions.explanation: Regression test selection picks the subset of existing tests that exercise changed code; unlike prioritization it omits tests, so safety analysis must guarantee none selected-out test could fail.
